root_cause.text: The BPF devmap XDP broadcast exclusion path used `get_upper_ifindexes()` to copy all upper-device ifindexes into a fixed-size stack array without enforcing a capacity limit, so devices with more than `MAX_NEST_DEV` uppers could overrun `excluded_devices` and cause a stack-out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch states that `get_upper_ifindexes()` “iterates over all upper devices and writes their indices into an array without checking bounds,” and that callers allocated `excluded_devices[1+MAX_NEST_DEV]` on the stack based on an invalid assumption; the fix adds a `max` parameter, checks `if (n >= max) return -EOVERFLOW;`, and updates `dev_map_enqueue_multi()` / `dev_map_redirect_multi()` to abort when too many upper devices are present.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The BPF devmap XDP broadcast exclusion path used `get_upper_ifindexes()` to copy all upper-device ifindexes into a fixed-size stack array without enforcing a capacity limit, so devices with more than `MAX_NEST_DEV` uppers could overrun `excluded_devices` and cause a stack-out-of-bounds write.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch states that `get_upper_ifindexes()` “iterates over all upper devices and writes their indices into an array without checking bounds,” and that callers allocated `excluded_devices[1+MAX_NEST_DEV]` on the stack based on an invalid assumption; the fix adds a `max` parameter, checks `if (n >= max) return -EOVERFLOW;`, and updates `dev_map_enqueue_multi()` / `dev_map_redirect_multi()` to abort when too many upper devices are present.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checking to `get_upper_ifindexes()` and return `-EOVERFLOW` when the upper-device list exceeds the caller's buffer.
intent_record.what: The function `get_upper_ifindexes()` was changed to take an additional `int max` parameter, its comment was updated to say the destination array must hold at least `max` elements, and the loop now checks `if (n >= max)` before writing. If the limit is exceeded, it returns `-EOVERFLOW` instead of continuing to append indices. A blank line was also added before the return.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now enforces the caller-provided output buffer capacity while collecting upper device ifindexes. This prevents writing past the end of the `indexes` array when a device has more upper devices than the buffer can hold, and it reports the overflow condition explicitly via `-EOVERFLOW`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the excluded device list capacity and propagate errors from get_upper_ifindexes() before adding the receive device index.
intent_record.what: The call to get_upper_ifindexes() was changed to pass a third argument, ARRAY_SIZE(excluded_devices) - 1, and the return value is now checked for a negative error code before dev_rx->ifindex is appended to excluded_devices.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now limits how many upper interface indexes can be collected to leave room for dev_rx itself, and it aborts early if get_upper_ifindexes() reports an error instead of continuing with a potentially invalid count.

intent_record.intent_summary: Limit excluded device collection and propagate errors from `get_upper_ifindexes()` in `dev_map_redirect_multi()`.
intent_record.what: The call to `get_upper_ifindexes()` was changed to pass a third argument, `ARRAY_SIZE(excluded_devices) - 1`, and the return value is now checked for `< 0`; on error, `dev_map_redirect_multi()` returns that error immediately before appending `dev->ifindex` to `excluded_devices`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now limits how many upper interface indexes can be collected and propagates failures from `get_upper_ifindexes()` instead of continuing with invalid data. This prevents overflow or misuse of the exclusion array and avoids building a redirect exclusion list when index collection fails.

grouping_result.intent: Limit excluded device collection and propagate errors from `get_upper_ifindexes()` in `dev_map_redirect_multi()`.

consistency_review.core_intent: Prevent buffer overflow and improve error propagation when collecting upper device indexes for excluded-device handling in dev_map_redirect_multi() and related helpers.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: unsafe copying of upper-device ifindexes into a fixed-size excluded_devices buffer. Adding bounds checks, clamping capacity, and returning -EOVERFLOW prevents the stack out-of-bounds write.

candidates.rationale: This writes each upper-device ifindex into the caller-provided stack array without any bounds check, which can overrun the fixed-size buffer when more than MAX_NEST_DEV uppers exist.

This appends the receive device index after collecting upper-device indexes, but if get_upper_ifindexes() already filled the fixed-size array past capacity, this write can land out of bounds and trigger the stack overflow.
This has the same unsafe append pattern as the ingress-exclusion path; if the upper-device collection overran the fixed-size array, this subsequent write can also occur out of bounds.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line copies each upper-device ifindex into the caller-provided fixed-size stack array without checking capacity, which is the root cause of the out-of-bounds write when the number of upper devices exceeds MAX_NEST_DEV.

This appends the receive device ifindex after collecting upper-device indexes; if the prior collection already overflowed the fixed-size array, this write can also land out of bounds and contribute to the stack overflow.
This is the same unsafe append pattern in the multi-redirect path, and it can write past the fixed-size excluded_devices array if the upper-device collection exceeded capacity.
